messages.subject: PDF File
parts:
GGPLOT2,

I am relatively new to ggplot2, but I was recently helped with developing the code below.  I was wondering, if there is a way one can save the output graph as a pdf file. 

Thanks,

Luciano

BiasF <- rbind(
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,1], fun = 'Bias of F unweighted'),
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,3], fun = 'Bias of F weighted'),
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,5], fun = 'Bias of F unweighted KM'),
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,7], fun = 'Bias of F weighted KM')
   )

ggplot(BiasF, aes(s, F, colour = fun, shape = fun)) +
   geom_point() + ylab('Bias') + xlab('Quantiles') +
   opts(labels = c(colour = 'Bias', shape = 'Bias'),
   title= 'Bias of Exponential for F')
key <- simpleKey(c(paste('n = ', n), paste('m = ', m), paste('N = ', N),
   paste('Frate = ', Frate), paste('Grate = ', Grate), paste('Rate1 = ', RATE1),
   paste('Rate2 = ', RATE2), paste('CenRate1 % = ', Rate1Per),
   paste('CenRate2 % = ', Rate2Per)), points = FALSE)
seekViewport("legend_box")
pushViewport(viewport(just=c(.525, .725)))
draw.key(key, draw=TRUE)

--

messages.subject: Re: PDF File
parts:
Hi Luciano -

You should be able to use the pdf() command and then dev.off() at the end, as follows :

BiasF <- rbind(
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,1], fun = 'Bias of F unweighted'),
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,3], fun = 'Bias of F weighted'),
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,5], fun = 'Bias of F unweighted KM'),
   data.frame(s = qF, F = sumBias[,7], fun = 'Bias of F weighted KM')
   )

ggplot(BiasF, aes(s, F, colour = fun, shape = fun)) + 
   geom_point() + ylab('Bias') + xlab('Quantiles') + 
   opts(labels = c(colour = 'Bias', shape = 'Bias'), 
   title= 'Bias of Exponential for F')
key <- simpleKey(c(paste('n = ', n), paste('m = ', m), paste('N = ', N), 
   paste('Frate = ', Frate), paste('Grate = ', Grate), paste('Rate1 = ', RATE1),
   paste('Rate2 = ', RATE2), paste('CenRate1 % = ', Rate1Per),
   paste('CenRate2 % = ', Rate2Per)), points = FALSE)
seekViewport("legend_box")
pushViewport(viewport(just=c(.525, .725)))
draw.key(key, draw=TRUE)

dev.off()


However, have you considered something like the following?

df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:10,
  class = rep(letters[1:2], each = 5)
)

qplot(x, x, data = df, colour = class) + 
  scale_colour_discrete(
    breaks = c('a','b'),
    labels = c('\nA\nn=50\n','\nB\nn=100\n')
  )

  

It may do what you want, and even though it's a rig it's a lot easier.

Hope it helps
david.

messages.subject: Re: PDF File
parts:
In my view, ggsave() is much easier to use:
myplot <- ggplot(...
ggsave('myplot.pdf", myplot)

Plus, that works even if you don't want to ever display myplot on the
screen.

Also, I don't think it's a good idea to suggest a beginner to ggplot
ever use qplot(). It leads to misunderstandings about what ggplot is
and does, and what ggplot objects are and how they're constructed. All
the syntactic sugar that's available is very misleading and prevents
the intuitions that make the grammar of graphics so powerful.

-Harlan
